proposal.reactor_type: Coiled-tube photoreactor (transparent PFA tubing wrapped around cylindrical LED array)
proposal.residence_time_basis: Reactor volume divided by total liquid volumetric flow rate; gas contribution to void volume is accounted for separately (see residence_time_in_channel_min).
proposal.light_setup: Cylindrical LED array (6 × 1.5 W LEDs, 9 W total optical power) surrounding the coiled PFA reactor; LEDs centered at 420 nm; reactor coil sits 5–10 mm from LED surface for uniform irradiation; total photon flux ~3× batch value to compensate for shorter path length and ensure complete conversion.

streams.pump_role: Primary reagent pump (HPLC or syringe pump)
streams.notes: Concentration set to 0.111 M so that after mixing with air stream the effective substrate concentration in the reactor is 0.10 M. Catalyst is 0.0111 M (10 mol%). Solution prepared fresh; protect from ambient light before entering reactor.

streams.molar_equiv: Large excess (O2 is the terminal oxidant; ~0.21 × 0.05 mL/min × P_correction provides dissolved O2 well above stoichiometric need for 1-electron oxidation of Met to Met-sulfoxide)
streams.notes: STP flow = 50 sccm. At 3.5 bar absolute back-pressure and 21 °C, ideal-gas compression gives in-channel volumetric flow ≈ 50/3.5 × (294/273) ≈ 14.6 mL/min STP-equivalent compressed to ~0.014 mL/min actual liquid-equivalent void volume. Slug-flow (Taylor flow) regime is targeted; gas:liquid volumetric ratio at inlet ≈ 0.05/0.45 ≈ 0.11, which is within the slug-flow window for 1 mm ID PFA. BPR keeps gas dissolved/segmented and prevents flash-off.

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK, 0.5 mm bore) followed by 5 cm pre-mix PFA line before reactor coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: S1 (liquid substrate/catalyst) enters one arm of the T-mixer; S2 (air) enters the other arm. Gas is introduced into the liquid stream at the T-junction to generate Taylor (slug) flow immediately. This maximises gas–liquid interfacial area for O2 mass transfer into the liquid phase, which is the key requirement for this aerobic photooxidation. The short pre-mix line (5 cm, ~0.03 mL dead volume) allows slug-flow pattern to stabilise before the illuminated zone. No pre-mixing of gas with substrate before the T is needed because the photocatalyst requires light to activate O2; premature dark mixing would waste dissolved O2 without productive reaction.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare stock solution of Fmoc-L-methionine (0.111 M) and 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (0.0111 M) in dry MeCN; degas briefly with N2 to remove adventitious moisture but do NOT fully degas (O2 will be supplied via S2).
Prime all tubing with MeCN before introducing substrate solution to avoid concentration transients.
Set MFC to 50 sccm air; verify BPR set-point at 3.5 bar; confirm LED array is at operating temperature (allow 5 min warm-up).
Run system at operating conditions with pure MeCN for 2 min to establish steady-state pressure and flow before switching to substrate solution.
post_reactor_steps: Effluent passes through BPR (3.5 bar) which separates residual gas from liquid; gas vented to fume hood exhaust.
Liquid effluent collected in amber vial on ice (0–5 °C) to prevent further oxidation to sulfone.
Discard first 1 reactor-volume (~2.5 mL) as non-steady-state fraction.
Analytical check: HPLC-UV (254 nm) or LC-MS to confirm ≥95% conversion to Fmoc-Met-sulfoxide and absence of sulfone by-product.
If sulfone detected (>2%), reduce residence time to 4 min or lower light intensity.
Solvent removal under reduced pressure (rotary evaporator, 30 °C, <20 mbar) if isolation required; product is stable as solid.
proposal.chemistry_notes: The reaction is a photocatalytic aerobic sulfoxidation. The 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole absorbs at ~420 nm and acts as a singlet-oxygen (¹O₂) sensitiser or electron-transfer photocatalyst; O2 is the terminal oxidant converting the thioether of methionine to the sulfoxide. The reaction is highly chemoselective (sulfoxide, not sulfone) under mild conditions (21 °C, air atmosphere, short irradiation). Key flow advantages: (1) enhanced O2 mass transfer via Taylor-flow gas–liquid segmentation; (2) precise irradiation time control (residence time = reaction time); (3) elimination of hot-spot overoxidation risk; (4) scalability by numbering-up. Fmoc group is stable under these conditions. MeCN is the preferred solvent (good photocatalyst solubility, transparent at 420 nm, compatible with Fmoc chemistry).

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Directly taken from batch protocol (5 min irradiation gave 99% yield). In flow, mass-transfer enhancement via Taylor flow may allow slightly shorter times, but 5 min is used as the conservative starting point to ensure equivalent conversion.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total liquid flow = 0.45 mL/min (S1) + negligible liquid equivalent of gas. Reactor volume 2.5 mL / 0.50 mL/min total ≈ 5 min. Chosen to be practical for HPLC-grade syringe or peristaltic pumps and to give a reactor volume <5 mL (easy to fabricate from standard PFA tubing).
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Matches batch (21 °C, ambient). No heating required; photocatalytic reaction is not thermally activated. Cooling coil on reactor not needed but ambient temperature control (±2 °C) recommended to avoid LED-induced heating.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.10 M matches batch. S1 is prepared at 0.111 M so dilution by gas stream (≈10% volumetric) gives 0.10 M effective concentration in reactor.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 3.5 bar absolute (≈2.5 bar gauge) chosen to: (1) keep O2 partially dissolved (Henry's law: higher pressure increases dissolved O2 concentration, improving mass transfer); (2) maintain Taylor flow without excessive bubble coalescence; (3) remain well within PFA tubing pressure rating (>10 bar). At 3.5 bar, dissolved O2 in MeCN ≈ 3× atmospheric value, providing ample oxidant.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Coiled PFA tube photoreactor is the standard choice for flow photochemistry: transparent to visible light, chemically inert to MeCN and Fmoc substrates, flexible for coiling, commercially available.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA selected over FEP (slightly better optical clarity at 420 nm) and over glass (fragility, cost). PFA transmits >90% at 420 nm for 1 mm wall thickness.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID: (1) gives Taylor flow at the chosen gas:liquid ratio; (2) short optical path length ensures uniform photon penetration (Beer-Lambert: at 0.10 M catalyst with ε ~10,000 M⁻¹cm⁻¹, absorbance over 0.5 mm radius ≈ 0.5, acceptable); (3) standard size for flow chemistry.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: V = π × (0.05 cm)² × L. For 2.5 mL: L = 2.5 / (π × 0.0025) ≈ 318 cm ≈ 3.2 m of tubing. Achievable as a compact coil (10 cm diameter, ~10 turns). Consistent with flow_rate × residence_time = 0.50 × 5 = 2.5 mL.
reasoning_per_field.gas_flow_sccm: 50 sccm air provides gas:liquid volumetric ratio of ~0.11 at inlet (before compression), targeting Taylor flow. Excess O2 ensures the reaction is not O2-limited. Actual in-channel gas volume is compressed by BPR pressure.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: 420 nm matches batch protocol and the absorption maximum of 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (literature λmax ~410–430 nm).
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer preferred over Y-mixer for gas–liquid systems; 0.5 mm bore creates sufficient velocity for slug formation at these flow rates.

literature_analogies: Plutschack et al., Chem. Rev. 2017, 117, 11796 – general principles of flow photochemistry, Taylor flow for gas–liquid reactions.
Knowles & Jamison, Acc. Chem. Res. 2012 – photocatalytic aerobic oxidations in flow.
Su et al., Org. Lett. 2014 – aerobic sulfoxidation using organic photocatalysts; confirms 420 nm sensitiser compatibility.
Loubière et al., Chem. Eng. Process. 2016 – LED photoreactor design for coiled-tube systems; optical power scaling.
Noël et al., React. Chem. Eng. 2019 – gas–liquid Taylor flow photochemistry in PFA microreactors; BPR strategy for O2 delivery.
safety_flags: ACETONITRILE – flammable (flash point 2 °C), toxic (TLV-TWA 40 ppm); use in fume hood; ground all metal fittings to prevent static discharge; keep away from ignition sources.
COMPRESSED AIR + ORGANIC SOLVENT – risk of flammable atmosphere if gas–liquid separator fails; install flame arrestor on gas vent line; verify BPR integrity before each run.
FMOC-L-METHIONINE – irritant; handle with gloves; no specific acute hazard but avoid inhalation of powder during weighing.
4,7-DIPHENYL-2,1,3-BENZOTHIADIAZOLE – limited toxicology data; treat as irritant; avoid skin/eye contact; dispose as organic waste.
SINGLET OXYGEN (¹O₂) – generated in situ; highly reactive oxidant; do not allow effluent to accumulate in closed containers before gas venting; keep collection vessel open or vented.
LED ARRAY (9 W, 420 nm) – violet/near-UV light; wear UV-blocking safety glasses rated for 400–450 nm; enclose reactor in opaque housing during operation.

PRESSURE – system operates at 3.5 bar; inspect all fittings and BPR before each run; do not exceed rated pressure of PFA tubing (typically >10 bar for 1 mm ID); install pressure relief valve rated at 6 bar upstream of reactor.
OVEROXIDATION HAZARD – prolonged residence time or excess light can convert sulfoxide to sulfone; monitor effluent by TLC or inline UV; implement automated flow-stop if conversion exceeds target.
WASTE DISPOSAL – MeCN/product mixture: collect as halogen-free organic solvent waste; do not combine with halogenated waste streams.

confidence.notes: High confidence on reaction translation (direct batch-to-flow analogy with well-precedented photocatalytic aerobic sulfoxidation). Moderate uncertainty on exact gas flow rate needed for optimal Taylor flow (requires experimental optimisation of gas:liquid ratio between 0.05–0.3); BPR pressure is a reasonable starting estimate. LED power scaled heuristically; photon-flux matching to batch should be verified by actinometry.
